article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Lemon Cherry Gelato × GSC × OG
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Company
THC Content: 25–30%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: limonene , caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Glazed doughnut, sugary pastry, vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October 5–10
Indoor Yield: 450–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 450–750 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Donutz is a modern dessert weed strain that actually smells as though its name came after the flower rather than before it. Humboldt Seed Company developed this balanced hybrid from Lemon Cherry Gelato, GSC, and OG genetics, producing dense green-and-purple marijuana flowers covered with enough resin to give the surface a glazed appearance. The aroma builds around sugary baked dough, vanilla, cinnamon, and cream before an unmistakable ribbon of fuel cuts through the sweetness.

Behind that confectionery profile sits considerable potency: Humboldt Seed Company’s European catalog places average THC around 25–30%, while the breeder describes the effect as laid-back, creative, social, and relaxing. The combination gives Donutz broad appeal—modern enough for consumers chasing dessert terpenes, yet sufficiently gassy and powerful to avoid becoming one-dimensional.
Genetics and Lineage

The official parentage is Lemon Cherry Gelato × GSC × OG. Humboldt Seed Company identifies the cultivar as a true 50/50 hybrid and lists its stabilization as S2 × DNZ #4, reflecting additional selection beyond simply making the initial cross. The genetic combination brings together three enormously influential branches of contemporary American cannabis. Lemon Cherry Gelato supplies vivid fruit, creamy sweetness, color, and modern resin-heavy flower structure; GSC contributes density, dessert-like complexity, and hybrid potency; OG reinforces the deeper fuel, earth, and physical relaxation beneath the sweeter aromatic surface.

That layered ancestry explains why the finished weed does not taste like straightforward pastry. A sweeter phenotype may emphasize glazed dough, vanilla, and cinnamon, while another can reveal considerably more gasoline and earthy OG character. The Lemon Cherry Gelato side can also encourage purple coloration as flowers mature, particularly when nighttime temperatures decline late in bloom. GSC and OG genetics help anchor those brighter traits with heavier resin production and a more substantial body component in the high.

Humboldt Seed Company has continued stabilizing Donutz rather than treating it as an unworked novelty cross. The breeder’s S2 × DNZ #4 designation indicates selection around a favored Donutz expression, helping reinforce the frosty flowers, consistent structure, sweet-fuel aroma, and balanced effect associated with the cultivar.
Effects and Experience

Donutz begins with a noticeably cerebral shift. Mood tends to improve first, followed by a sense of mental looseness that can make conversation, music, creative projects, or social activities more engaging. Humboldt Seed Company characterizes the experience as creative and social, and that description fits the early portion particularly well. The high can feel upbeat without becoming aggressively stimulating, giving the cultivar a more relaxed tone than many sativa-dominant varieties.

Physical calm gradually develops underneath the mental lift. Muscular tension can soften, movement becomes less urgent, and the initial excitement settles into an easygoing state without necessarily producing immediate couch-lock. At moderate doses, that balance makes the strain versatile enough for late afternoons, evenings, or relaxed gatherings. Larger amounts expose more of its potency and can shift the experience toward heavier physical relaxation.

THC around 25–30% places Donutz firmly in high-potency territory according to Humboldt Seed Company’s European specifications. That range makes dose control important, particularly for newer consumers. A flower carrying nearly 30% THC can turn pleasant creative stimulation into dizziness, anxiety, or excessive sedation when consumed too quickly.
Medical Benefits

The transition from elevated mood into physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers seeking a versatile THC-dominant cultivar. Some people favor this type of weed during periods of temporary stress, low mood, mental fatigue, or physical tension because it can provide an uplifting beginning without remaining intensely energetic for the entire session.

There is no controlled clinical evidence showing that Donutz itself treats anxiety, depression, chronic pain, insomnia, PTSD, or another medical condition. Strain-specific medical claims should therefore remain conservative. Even plants carrying identical genetics can differ chemically depending on environment, maturity, curing, and phenotype.

With CBD generally low and THC potentially approaching 30%, this is not a balanced cannabinoid cultivar. Consumers particularly sensitive to THC may find lower-potency cannabis or THC/CBD-balanced flower easier to manage. Laboratory information from the actual harvested batch remains more useful medically than the strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The breeder’s description of glazed doughnuts is unusually accurate. Mature flowers produce sweet dough, vanilla, and cinnamon notes that can suggest a bakery rather than fresh fruit alone. Humboldt Seed Company specifically characterizes the profile as glazed donuts and sugary dough with hints of fuel. Dense resin intensifies the aroma when a bud is broken apart, releasing creamier sweetness alongside sharper petroleum and earthy cannabis notes.

Flavor develops in layers. Sweet pastry and vanilla frequently appear on the inhale, followed by cinnamon-like spice and creamy dough. The exhale brings more OG-style fuel and earth, preventing the cultivar from becoming cloyingly sweet. Some phenotypes may retain traces of cherry or citrus from Lemon Cherry Gelato, while others emphasize gasoline and spice.

Humboldt Seed Company does not publish one fixed terpene hierarchy for every Donutz plant. Contemporary listings associated with the genetics include compounds such as limonene, caryophyllene, myrcene, pinene, and linalool, but those ratios are best treated as sample-specific rather than permanent characteristics.
Growing Information

Donutz was selected to be relatively straightforward in the garden. Humboldt Seed Company describes strong plants with average internodal spacing and rates performance highly across indoor, outdoor, greenhouse, and light-deprivation environments. That intermediate spacing is useful because flowers receive better light penetration than they would on an extremely compact plant, yet the canopy does not develop the uncontrolled stretch seen in many long-flowering sativas.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 55–60 days, making Donutz unusually fast for a balanced, high-potency hybrid. Outdoor harvest is listed around October 5–10. Dense nodular flowers become extremely frosty as maturity approaches, often displaying green and purple coloration. Indoor production around 450–600 g/m² is a reasonable target under efficient lighting, while outdoor plants may reach approximately 450–750 g each under favorable conditions. Those figures depend heavily on root space, vegetative time, nutrition, climate, and canopy management.

Topping and low-stress training can help spread productive branches across the light footprint, although excessive intervention is rarely necessary. Humidity deserves more attention late in bloom because dense resinous flowers can retain moisture. Humboldt Seed Company also includes Donutz among its mold-resistant photoperiod cultivars, an advantage for greenhouse and outdoor growers, though resistance should never be mistaken for immunity.
FAQ
Is Donutz an indica or sativa?

Donutz is a balanced hybrid. Humboldt Seed Company classifies it as approximately 50% indica and 50% sativa, which matches its combination of uplifting cerebral effects and progressively stronger physical relaxation.
What are the genetics of Donutz?
The official parentage is Lemon Cherry Gelato × GSC × OG. Humboldt Seed Company also lists the stabilized seed line as S2 × DNZ #4.
How much THC does Donutz have?

Humboldt Seed Company’s European catalog gives an average THC range of approximately 25–30%. Actual cannabis flower may test above or below that range depending on phenotype and cultivation conditions.
What does Donutz taste like?
The defining flavors are glazed doughnuts, sugary pastry, vanilla, cinnamon, and fuel. Some examples also reveal cream, cherry, citrus, and earthy OG notes underneath the bakery-like sweetness.
How long does Donutz take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally requires approximately 55–60 days. Humboldt Seed Company places outdoor maturity around October 5–10 under suitable Northern Hemisphere conditions.
Final Thoughts on Donutz

Donutz demonstrates how far modern dessert cannabis has progressed from simply breeding for sweetness. Lemon Cherry Gelato, GSC, and OG give Humboldt Seed Company’s cultivar enough genetic depth to combine genuine pastry aromatics with high THC, dense resin production, balanced effects, and practical garden performance. Vanilla, cinnamon, sugary dough, and cream dominate the sweeter side, while fuel and earth keep the finished flower rooted firmly in potent California weed.

Cultivators also get unusually convenient characteristics for such premium-looking marijuana: roughly 55–60 days of flowering, manageable internodal spacing, strong performance across several growing environments, and good mold resistance. For consumers, the experience moves naturally from upbeat creativity and sociability toward relaxed physical calm. Donutz may have a playful name, but the genetics and breeding work behind it make the strain much more substantial than another temporary dessert-flavor trend.
